'The best' is the superlative form of the adjective 'good'.
bank.template: This is {{0}} fish and chips I have ever eaten in this town.

bank.explanation: 'Taking up' is a phrasal verb that means starting a new hobby or activity.
bank.template: I am thinking about {{0}} gardening because I have a lot of space in my backyard.
I need to go {{0}} the GP surgery to pick up my prescription.
bank.explanation: We use 'go to' when referring to movement towards a specific location or destination.

bank.template: Please {{0}} your shoes before you enter the flat.
bank.explanation: 'Take off' is a phrasal verb meaning to remove a piece of clothing or footwear.

bank.template: My sister {{0}} a book when her mobile phone suddenly rang.
bank.explanation: The past continuous 'was reading' is used for an action in progress when a shorter action (the phone ringing) happened.
'Who' is a relative pronoun used to provide more information about a person.
bank.template: The woman {{0}} lives next door works as a nurse at the local hospital.

bank.explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'traffic' in negative sentences and questions.
bank.template: There isn't {{0}} traffic on the M1 motorway this morning.
Did you {{0}} the news about the new shopping centre last night?
bank.explanation: The phrase 'Did you' is followed by the base form of the verb to ask questions in the past simple.

bank.template: I {{0}} my homework yet, so I cannot go to the park.
bank.explanation: The present perfect 'haven't finished' is used with 'yet' to describe an action not completed up to now.
'Taller than' is the comparative form used to compare two people or things.
bank.template: My brother is slightly {{0}} me, but I am stronger.
You {{0}} pay for the museum entry because it is free on Sundays.
bank.explanation: 'Don't have to' is used to show that there is no obligation or necessity to do something.

bank.prompt: Choose the correct passive voice form.
bank.explanation: The passive voice 'was built' is used to describe an action done to the subject (the house) in the past.
bank.template: This beautiful old terrace house {{0}} over a hundred years ago.
I {{0}} my aunt in Birmingham this weekend for her birthday.
bank.explanation: The present continuous 'am visiting' is used to describe a definite arrangement or plan in the near future.
The verb 'suggested' is followed by the '-ing' form (gerund) when suggesting an action.
bank.template: The council suggested {{0}} more bike racks to encourage cycling in the city.
